records.c: A pointer the copies and drawing routines share, low byte first ($02-$03): the source of a block copy, or the bitmap address a new column goes to.
The high byte of ptr_a.
A second shared pointer ($04-$05): the destination of a block copy, or the screen address a new column's colours go to.
The high byte of ptr_b.
Where the next colour cell is read from in the pool's colour map at $1000, low byte first ($06-$07); a row is 100 bytes on.
The high byte of map_ptr.
The screen address the start-up build writes a colour row to ($08-$09).
The high byte of scr_ptr.
A sprite's x position on the screen, low byte, as sprite placement works it out.
The ninth bit of spr_x, which decides the sprite's bit in $D010.
A sprite's y position, as sprite placement works it out.
A group's pool x, plus 20 for the first swimmer's, low byte, while it is checked against the camera.
The high byte of grp_px.
The destination pointer of the loader stub's copy, low byte first ($10-$11); the start-up build also uses it as a colour-RAM pointer.
The high byte of copy_dst.
A counter: rows still to draw or players still to list; the result writer also uses it and $13 as a scratch pair for a time.
The second byte of count when it holds a time or a pointer.
Not used by this part ($14-$15).
Not used by this part either.
The x position of the sprite group being placed, low byte.
The high byte of grp_x.
The y position of the sprite group being placed.
The index into the frame tables of the sprite being placed; it steps on by one for each sprite of a group.
The raster list being worked through, low byte first ($1A-$1B): pairs of handler and next line, ended by a zero.
The high byte of irq_list.
The raster list to change to when the current one ends, low byte first ($1C-$1D); $1D is cleared once the change is made.
The high byte of irq_next, and the flag set_irq_list waits on.
The offset in irq_list of the line the next interrupt comes on.
Not zero while the results screen is showing, so the line-3 handler turns the text screen on.
The new column's colour-RAM colours for rows 4 to 8 ($20-$24), which draw_left and draw_right fill from tile_colram and the colour shift puts in place.
The new column's colour-RAM colour for row 5.
The new column's colour-RAM colour for row 6.
The new column's colour-RAM colour for row 7.
The new column's colour-RAM colour for row 8.
The new column's colour-RAM colours for rows 9 to 23 ($25-$33).
The first swimmer's colour, from the player's number through player_col.
The second swimmer's colour.
The fine scroll, 0 to 7, the low three bits of $D016.
The pool's value for $D016, multicolour and the fine scroll, kept here while the panel above shows without either.
The value for $DD00 that picks the buffer the pool is shown from: 2 for bank 1 ($4000) or 3 for bank 0.
The value for $D018 that goes with vic_bank: $78 for bank 1, $38 for bank 0.
The camera's position in the pool, in pixels, low byte first ($3F-$40).
The high byte of cam_x.
The screen x positions of the four sprite groups, low bytes ($41-$44): the first swimmer on the blocks, the second on the blocks, the first in the water, the second in the water.
The high bytes of grp_sx ($45-$48).
The y positions of the four sprite groups ($49-$4C).
The first frame index of each sprite group ($4D-$50), into the tables at $F783 to $F923.
The sprite-enable bits for each group, or 0 when it is off the screen ($51-$54).
The pool x positions behind the groups, low bytes ($55-$58): $55-$56 the swimmers on the blocks and diving, $57-$58 the swimmers in the water.
The high bytes of obj_x ($59-$5C).
Each swimmer's animation counter ($5D-$5E), cleared when it reaches the speed's count in anim_rate.
Each swimmer's speed ($5F-$60): 1 on the blocks, 4 after the dive, 0 to 7 as the strokes change it, 8 when held back to keep up, 12 in a turn and 15 pushing off.
The speed a swimmer had before a turn, given back after it ($61-$62).
Each swimmer's step, 1 or -1 ($63-$64), negated at each wall.
Each swimmer's direction ($65-$66): 0 up the pool, $FF back.
Each swimmer's stroke counter ($67-$68); the stroke moves on when it reaches the speed's count in stroke_rate.
Each swimmer's turn ($69-$6A): 0 none, $FF at the far wall waiting for the turn, 1 turning.
The fire-button samples taken during a stroke, one bit each ($6B-$6C), which decide the change in speed.
Each swimmer's false starts ($6D-$6E); the third sets it to $FF, disqualified.
Each swimmer's place in the race ($6F-$70): 0 out of it, 1 named, $FF ready; in the relay $FF also marks a swimmer due to hand over at the next wall.
Each swimmer's dive phase ($71-$72): $FF on the blocks, 1 to 9 diving, 0 in the water.
The forward step of the dive phase, an index into dive_steps ($73-$74).
Not zero while a swimmer is swimming ($75-$76).
Frames left in a dive phase, or of the glide after a turn ($77-$78).
Walls each swimmer has turned at or touched ($79-$7A).
The wall counts the race loop last acted on ($7B-$7C).
$FF while a race is running; 0 after a false start, until the swimmers are back on the blocks.
The pool column at the left edge of the screen, 0 to 80.
The six sprite pointers of the clock ($7F-$84): minutes, colon, tens of seconds, seconds, point, tenths.
The colon's pointer, $34.
The decimal point's pointer, $35.
Frames since the clock last moved, 0 to 5.
Not zero while the clock runs.
Counts races ended; nothing reads it.
Set when a race has started, so the next start clears the clock.
Not zero when a swimmer has finished: the clock runs on but the display keeps the first finisher's time.
The clock's hundredths, BCD; it moves by ten at a time.
The clock's seconds, BCD, 0 to 59.
The clock's minutes, 0 to 9.
Set when a scroll starts, so the race loop draws the first new column at once; cleared when a column is drawn.
Set by the frame handler when the fine scroll wraps and the buffers swap: the colours must shift and the next column be drawn.
The number of players less one.
The number of the first player in the race under way; a race takes one or two players.
Picks the pair of bytes in each player's eight at $1CC0; nothing sets it, so it stays 0 from the clear.
Counts frames; the waits clear it and watch it.
The scroll under way: 0 none, 1 the camera moving right, up the pool, 8 moving left.
The scroll the camera starts when a swimmer reaches the edge; flipped when a scroll ends.
The first swimmer's fire button, 0 when pressed ($95), and the second's at $96.
The first swimmer's joystick right, 0 when pushed ($97), and the second's at $98.
The first swimmer's joystick left, 0 when pushed ($9A), and the second's at $9B.
How far into the wall a swimmer was when the turn was asked for ($9C-$9D), which picks the glide.
Five bytes the event table gives ($9E-$A2): the title's address, the finishing mask and the wall count of a hand-over.
$FE for the 100 metres, so two walls end it; $F8 for the relay, so eight end it.
The wall count at the last leg's far turn: 6 for the relay, so the earlier legs hand over at the near wall; 0 for the 100 metres, whose one turn has none.
The value put in $D015 for the clock's sprites.
Bit 7 set at $E055 once the machine's pages have been saved; the clear at $E0B7 zeroes it again.
Extra steps each swimmer takes this frame ($A8-$A9), from the speed change of a stroke.
Set when a swimmer off the screen is to be put back at its edge ($AA-$AB).
Not zero while each sprite group is on the screen ($AC-$AF).
Not zero once a swimmer has finished ($B0-$B3): the group is held at the near wall and shows this frame.
